html:
The Emirate of Diriyah, the first Saudi state, was founded in 1727 by Muhammad bin Saud, ruler of the small oasis town of Diriyah near today's Riyadh in central Arabia. It lasted until 1818.

In 1744 he made a pact with the preacher Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab: the Saud family would rule and spread his strict reform of Islam, and his teaching would back their rule. Their armies took most of Arabia, sacked the Shia shrine city of Karbala in 1802, and took Mecca and Medina in the early 1800s.

The Ottoman sultan sent the army of Egypt against them in the Ottoman-Wahhabi War, and Diriyah was destroyed in 1818. The pact of 1744 survived and was renewed by later Saudi states, down to Ibn Saud. See also Wahhabism.
